slides.texte_overlay:
7 social hacks that feel
like cheating at parties
Hold a drink, even if it's just water. It gives your hands something to do, it's an easy excuse to move around the room, and "I'm going for a refill, want one?" is the perfect way out of any chat.
Introduce two people who should know each other. "You both just got back from Japan, you need to talk." Then step back. Connecting people makes you look like the host, even when you're not.
Bring one good story to every party. Five minutes a day of history, art or science and you've got plenty. "Did you know the fortune cookie isn't actually Chinese?" The whole kitchen gathers round.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: standing in the kitchen with nothing to say. After: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app, and you've always got a story. "The fortune cookie isn't even Chinese."

slides.texte_overlay: Remember one detail about everyone you meet. The dog's name, the new job, the trip next week. Bring it up an hour later. "So when do you leave for Lisbon?" People feel seen, and they remember you.
Ask "What's keeping you busy these days?" instead of "What do you do?" It works on students, parents and people between jobs, and it gets you the interesting answer, not the job title.
Help the host clean up a little before you leave. Carry a few glasses to the kitchen, ask "Anything I can do?" It takes two minutes, and you'll be first on the list next time.
Leave while it's still fun. Don't wait for the lights to come on. Find the host, say thanks, and go. People always remember the guy who left on a high, not the one still there at 4am.
